newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA REJECT ENGLAND TEST DATE OFFER.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA REJECT ENGLAND TEST DATE OFFER.

text.p: The Australian Rugby Union (ARU) will meet on Monday in a bid to resolve a dispute with the British unions over the schedule for the Wallabies' tour of Europe later this year, media reports on Saturday said.

Australia and the British unions are locked in an increasingly intractable dispute over the possibility of adding a test against England to the Wallabies' eight-week, 13-match tour of Europe which starts in Italy on October 19.
The ARU on Friday described as "preposterous" an offer by Home Union Tour Committee (HUTC) chairman Bob Weighhill of the mid-week dates of December 3 or 4 for the England test.

The Wallabies had earlier suggested either November 2 or 16 for the England test and said they would consider cancelling the December 1 test against Wales at Cardiff, which had been added to their original itinerary, if those dates were rejected.
"Their offer is just a sham," ARU chief executive John O'Neill was quoted as saying in The Australian newspaper on Saturday.
"We've got a multi-million dollar Wallaby team that will be travelling around the backblocks of Scotland, yet they can't play England.
"I told (Weighhill) we would now be looking at the option of cancelling the Welsh test," he said.
Weighhill said on Friday the threat to drop the Wales test could have "serious repercussions", which in turn brought a stern response from O'Neill.
"The whole thing is just ridiculous," O'Neill told The Australian.
"This Four Home Unions Tours Committee is an anachronism. The sooner it's abolished the better," he said.
Weighhill said it was not easy to change arrangements which had been in place for up to six months.
"For many of those people this is a rugby event of a lifetime," he said.

"I can understand Australia's frustration but they should appreciate our problems. They also have to realise the game is in absolute turmoil over here with the dispute between the unions and professional clubs," Weighhill said.
Australia are scheduled to play Italy, Ireland, Scotland and Wales and hoped to add an England test so they could play their first "Grand Slam" of Home Unions matches since 1984.
